entries.title: The progression
entries.text: Insulin resistance, compensation, and beta-cell failure Insulin resistance Target tissues — muscle, fat, liver — respond poorly to insulin. Glucose is not taken up efficiently and the liver does not suppress its output as it should. Nothing is wrong with the beta cell yet. Compensatory hyperinsulinemia The beta cell answers resistance by secreting more insulin , and for a long while it succeeds: glucose stays normal at the cost of a rising insulin level. This is why a normal glucose does not mean a normal metabolism — and why C-peptide is high, not low , in T2DM. Beta-cell dysfunction The compensation is not sustainable. Secretory capacity declines, and the gap between what is needed and what is delivered opens. Insulin deficiency in T2DM is relative , not absolute — which is exactly why ketoacidosis is uncommon here and hyperosmolar states are not. Worsening hyperglycemia Glucose crosses the prediabetes range, then the diabetes threshold. By this point the process has been running for years — which is why microvascular complications are sometimes already present at the moment of diagnosis, and why screening at-risk people rather than waiting for symptoms matters so much. Genetics and environment T2DM has a strong genetic contribution , expressed through interaction with nutrition, activity, sleep, and other environmental factors. Recognize Who to suspect, what to look for, and what the labs show

entries.title: Suspicion and signs
entries.text: Clinical suspicion and physical findings Symptoms Polyuria, polydipsia, polyphagia — the same three Ps, because the mechanism downstream of the hyperglycemia is identical. Plus nocturia and nocturnal enuresis . The difference from T1DM is tempo : this often accumulates so gradually that the patient does not report it, and the diagnosis comes from a screening test rather than a complaint. Signs and history Acanthosis nigricans · overweight or obesity · family history , which carries particular weight given how strong the heritability is here. Look at the back of the neck and the axillae on anybody you are screening. Acanthosis nigricans — what it actually is Velvety, thickened, hyperpigmented skin in flexural areas: the back and sides of the neck, the axillae, the groin, sometimes the knuckles. It is not a hygiene problem and does not scrub off — a distinction worth making explicitly, because patients are frequently told otherwise. It is a visible marker of insulin resistance , and a recognized clinical sign of both prediabetes and T2DM. Finding it on examination should prompt a glucose or A1c, not reassurance. Hughes EK, Brady MF, Rawla P. Acanthosis Nigricans. StatPearls [Internet]. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing. ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK431057

entries.title: Screening and diagnosis
entries.text: Screening, prediabetes, and the diagnostic thresholds Diagnostic thresholds for prediabetes and diabetes Three tests shown as bands. Fasting plasma glucose: normal below 100, prediabetes 100 to 125, diabetes above 125 milligrams per deciliter. Two-hour glucose on an oral glucose tolerance test: normal below 140, prediabetes 140 to 199, diabetes above 199. HbA1c: normal below 5.7 percent, prediabetes 5.7 to 6.4 percent, diabetes above 6.4 percent. A random plasma glucose above 199 with symptoms is also diagnostic. Asymptomatic patients require two abnormal results on subsequent days. NORMAL · PREDIABETES · DIABETES Fasting plasma glucose (mg/dL) < 100 100 – 125 > 125 2-hour glucose on OGTT (mg/dL) < 140 140 – 199 > 199 HbA1c (%) < 5.7 5.7 – 6.4 > 6.4 TWO MORE RULES THAT QUESTIONS ARE BUILT ON · A random glucose > 199 mg/dL WITH SYMPTOMS is diagnostic on its own. · Asymptomatic patients need TWO abnormal results on subsequent days. Original figure. The conventional written forms of the same cut-points are fasting ≥126 mg/dL, 2-hour ≥200 mg/dL, and A1c ≥6.5% — the strict-inequality phrasing above describes the same boundaries. Bar widths are for legibility and are not to scale. Prediabetes / impaired glucose tolerance Defined by the middle band on all three tests. Acanthosis nigricans is a clinical sign at this stage too, and treatment is nutrition and exercise , with medication therapy as an option. The framing that matters: prediabetes is not a mild version of diabetes, it is a point on the curve where the trajectory can still be changed . Labs that support T2DM specifically Negative GAD-65 antibody, islet cell antibody, and insulin autoantibody. Elevated C-peptide and insulin. Read together: no autoimmunity, and plenty of endogenous insulin being made — the problem is that it is not working. Compare with T1DM , where C-peptide is low. American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee. 2. Diagnosis and Classification of Diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026. Diabetes Care. 2026;49(Suppl 1):S27–S49. doi:10.2337/dc26-S002 T1DM versus T2DM — the comparison the objectives ask for explicitly. Every row is a tendency, not a rule; see the classification exercise on the T1DM page . T1DM T2DM Core defect Autoimmune beta-cell destruction → absolute insulin deficiency Insulin resistance → beta-cell dysfunction → relative deficiency Autoantibodies Positive — GAD-65, ICA-512, IAA Negative C-peptide Low Normal or elevated Body habitus Often lean, with recent weight loss — but obesity does not exclude it Usually overweight or obesity, with central adiposity Acanthosis nigricans Not characteristic Characteristic Onset Weeks — catabolic, symptomatic, sometimes in DKA Years — often silent, often found on screening Family history May be present, but is less characteristic A close relative with diabetes is common Characteristic emergency DKA HHS — but neither is exclusive to one type Insulin required Always, from diagnosis, permanently Sometimes, and often later in the disease

entries.title: Metabolic syndrome
entries.text: Metabolic syndrome Also called insulin resistance syndrome, or syndrome X — named in Gerald Reaven's 1988 Banting Lecture as a cluster of effects downstream of hyperinsulinemia and insulin resistance. Metabolic syndrome as a hub around insulin resistance Abdominal obesity drives insulin resistance and hyperinsulinemia, which sits at the center. Radiating from it are central adiposity, raised blood pressure, high triglycerides, low HDL cholesterol, and hyperglycemia. Adipocyte cytokines feed back into the center. All of these converge on the ultimate threat, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Abdominal obesity BMI and weight are not the criterion Insulin resistance = hyperinsulinemia Central adiposity cytokines ↑ Blood pressure hypertension ↑ Trigly- cerides dyslipidemia ↓ HDL cholesterol dyslipidemia Hyper- glycemia → T2DM Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease the "ultimate threat" of the cluster THE DEADLY QUARTET Abdominal obesity · hyperglycemia · dyslipidemia (high TG, low HDL) · hypertension Original diagram of the pathway Reaven's framework describes. Note the causal direction: abdominal obesity drives insulin resistance , resistance produces hyperinsulinemia, and the cluster of features radiates from there rather than merely co-occurring. Reaven GM. Banting Lecture 1988. Role of insulin resistance in human disease. Diabetes. 1988;37(12):1595–1607. doi:10.2337/diab.37.12.1595 What insulin resistance produces Impaired peripheral glucose and fatty acid utilization · vascular endothelial dysfunction · impaired lipid metabolism · hypertension . Note that endothelial dysfunction appears here, at the metabolic-syndrome stage — before diabetes is diagnosed. The vascular disease does not wait for the glucose threshold. The detail that catches people Explicitly: BMI and weight are not a criterion — it is abdominal obesity that matters. Someone with a BMI in the normal range but central adiposity can meet the definition, and someone with a high BMI and a favorable fat distribution may not. The comorbidities that travel with T2DM Hypertension · dyslipidemia · fatty liver disease · chronic kidney disease · polycystic ovary syndrome · obstructive sleep apnea · hyperuricemia and gout · metabolic syndrome. Most share insulin resistance as a common root, which is why they cluster. Localize Separating the two hyperglycemic emergencies

entries.title: HHS, and HHS vs DKA
entries.text: Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state, and how it differs from DKA Diagnostic features Hyperglycemia — glucose above 600 mg/dL. Hyperosmolality — serum osmolality above 330 mOsm/kg. No acidosis , and the absence of significant ketosis . Those three together define it. Kitabchi AE, Umpierrez GE, Miles JM, Fisher JN. Hyperglycemic crises in adult patients with diabetes. Diabetes Care. 2009;32(7):1335–1343. doi:10.2337/dc09-9032 Why there are no ketones — the mechanistic heart of the topic HHS arises from relative insulin deficiency, with a rise in counter-regulatory hormones because glucose is not being used, and increased hepatic and renal glucose production through gluconeogenesis . The idea is worth memorizing almost verbatim: there is just enough circulating insulin to prevent lipolysis and the subsequent free fatty acid production, but not enough insulin to support adequate glucose utilization . Say it as a threshold problem Suppressing lipolysis takes less insulin than driving glucose into cells does. So as insulin availability falls, glucose uptake fails first while lipolysis stays switched off. The patient becomes profoundly hyperglycemic without making ketones. Only when insulin falls further — as in T1DM — does lipolysis get released and ketogenesis begin. One axis, two thresholds : that single idea explains why DKA and HHS are different presentations of the same hormone deficit, and why the type of diabetes predicts which one you tend to see without determining it. DKA versus HHS. Read the "insulin available" row first — every other difference follows from it. Feature DKA HHS Insulin available Essentially absent — absolute deficiency Present but insufficient — relative deficiency Degree of hyperglycemia Typically above 250 mg/dL — high, but usually less extreme Above 600 mg/dL — far higher Ketones Present , and central to the diagnosis Absent or insignificant Acidosis Anion-gap metabolic acidosis ; bicarbonate below 15, anion gap typically above 16 No acidosis Serum osmolality Raised Above 330 mOsm/kg — this is the defining derangement Dehydration Marked Profound — the osmotic diuresis has run for longer at a higher glucose Neurologic manifestations Altered mental status, usually tracking the acidosis Prominent — altered mental status tracking the osmolality, and often the presenting problem Breathing Kussmaul respirations , compensating for the acidosis Not a feature — there is no acidosis to compensate for Typically associated with T1DM T2DM, often an older patient Speed of onset Hours to a couple of days Days to weeks Neither emergency is exclusive to one type of diabetes Patients with T2DM can present with DKA , and older adults with T1DM can develop HHS. The associations in the last two rows above are typical , not defining. Diagnose the emergency from the glucose, the ketones, the acid–base status, and the osmolality — never from the label already in the chart. HHS complications Thrombosis — profound dehydration and hyperviscosity · rhabdomyolysis , and through it acute kidney injury, hyperkalemia, and hypocalcemia, which together can cause cardiac arrest · muscle swelling leading to compartment syndrome · malignant hyperthermia · cerebral edema . entries.title: Treatment approaches
entries.text: Treatment The point of this section is that there are many treatment modalities — the emphasis is on the categories and the lifestyle foundation, not on individual drug pharmacology. Nutrition and dietary counseling Weight stabilization , then weight loss — a widely used initial target is 7% of body weight · eliminate sugary beverages · encourage plant-based eating · and, importantly, identify the patient's dietary preferences . Named patterns: Mediterranean, low calorie, low fat, DASH, intermittent fasting. Medical nutrition therapy centers on no concentrated sugars and carbohydrate monitoring , with support from family, friends, school, and work. Exercise counseling Children: 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous aerobic activity per day. Adults: 150 minutes per week. Muscle- and bone-strengthening activity on 3 days per week for both. Screen-time counseling belongs alongside these, particularly for children and adolescents. Glucose monitoring Patient-specific. Options: fasting, pre-meal, and 2-hour post-prandial checks; standard basal-bolus monitoring at 4 times daily ; or continuous glucose monitoring . Medication categories Four broad modalities: oral medication , insulin therapy , oral medication plus insulin , and injectable glucose-lowering agents other than insulin. Insulin in T2DM is a tool used when the others are insufficient, not a sign of failure — a framing worth passing on to patients. American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee. Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026. Diabetes Care. 2026;49(Suppl 1). diabetesjournals.org/care/issue/49/Supplement_1 A scope note on pharmacology This page stays at the level of treatment categories . It does not work through the mechanisms, adverse effects, or comparative benefits of individual agents — metformin, sulfonylureas, SGLT2 inhibitors, GLP-1 receptor agonists, DPP-4 inhibitors, and the rest. Coursework cases mention specific drugs by name, so recognizing which category a named drug belongs to is reasonable to expect; detailed pharmacology is not covered here and this page does not manufacture it. One safety-relevant point does belong here , because it appears in the practice bank: among oral agents, the insulin secretagogues — the sulfonylureas, such as glipizide, glyburide, and glimepiride — can cause hypoglycemia , particularly when meals are missed or delayed, whereas metformin used alone does not.

entries.title: Chronic complications
entries.text: How chronic hyperglycemia damages tissue From chronic hyperglycemia to organ complications Chronic hyperglycemia acts through three mechanisms: advanced glycation end-products formed by non-enzymatic glycation, sorbitol accumulation via aldose reductase, and oxidative stress with inflammation. These converge on two vascular pathways. Microvascular injury produces retinopathy, nephropathy, and neuropathy. Endothelial dysfunction and accelerated atherosclerosis produce coronary artery disease, cerebrovascular disease, and peripheral arterial disease. Chronic hyperglycemia AGEs non-enzymatic glycation alters protein structure → permeability, stiffness, cytokines, ischemia Sorbitol accumulation aldose reductase makes it; no sorbitol dehydrogenase to clear it → osmotic and oxidative injury Oxidative stress and inflammation amplifies both of the other two pathways Microvascular injury small vessels, capillaries, nerves Endothelial dysfunction → accelerated atherosclerosis MICROVASCULAR · Retinopathy · Nephropathy · Neuropathy "the three -opathies" MACROVASCULAR · Coronary artery disease · Cerebrovascular disease · Peripheral arterial disease occlusion, thrombosis, gangrene Extent is determined by DURATION of diabetes and DEGREE of glucose control. Those are the two levers — one you cannot change, one you can. Original diagram tracing the standard damage mechanisms through to the named complications. Microvascular complications Retinopathy Retinal ischemia and neovascularization ; fragile new vessels can bleed and threaten vision. Nephropathy Albuminuria/proteinuria from glomerular injury; control glucose and blood pressure and screen for early disease. Neuropathy Sorbitol accumulation and AGE injury damage peripheral nerves and Schwann cells. Macrovascular complications Coronary artery, cerebrovascular, and peripheral arterial disease from endothelial dysfunction and accelerated atherosclerosis. entries.title: Basal versus bolus
entries.text: What insulin therapy is trying to reproduce Basal insulin restrains hepatic glucose output between meals and overnight; bolus insulin covers meals. Every regimen attempts to reproduce both jobs. A basal-bolus day Across a 24-hour day, a low continuous basal insulin level covers overnight and between-meal periods. Three carbohydrate loads at breakfast, lunch, and dinner each produce a rise in glucose demand, matched by a mealtime bolus given at each meal. A separate correction dose can be added to a mealtime bolus, or given on its own between meals, to bring an out-of-range glucose back toward target. BASAL — continuous background, overnight and between meals breakfast lunch dinner CARBOHYDRATE LOAD BOLUS — one per meal, sized to the carbohydrate CORRECTION — added to a meal bolus, or given alone 12a 8a 1p 6p 12a Two jobs, two kinds of insulin. A regimen that cannot separate them has to constrain the patient's day instead. When a glucose pattern is abnormal, identify which insulin was acting beforehand. The rule underneath everything T1DM requires insulin at all times, with no exceptions for illness or reduced intake. Basal insulin is not "the insulin for food," and it is not paused because someone is not eating. Without any insulin at all, the liver resumes ketogenesis regardless of what the patient has or has not eaten. Recognize The five categories, and what each one's shape means clinically

entries.title: Insulin action curves
entries.text: Insulin profiles Know the categories and the examples within each. The curves let you see why the category matters clinically, not just as a label. Rapid-acting Lispro (Humalog), aspart (NovoLog), glulisine (Apidra). On and off quickly, with an early peak — which is what lets it match a meal and then get out of the way. It is also the only insulin used in a pump. Regular — short-acting Regular human insulin (R). Slower on, and it lasts longer than the meal does. That tail is the reason regimens using regular insulin traditionally require timed snacks: the insulin outlives the food. NPH — intermediate NPH (N). A broad mid-range peak. That peak is both its usefulness — it can cover a meal several hours after injection — and its hazard, because a peak that arrives while the patient is asleep is a peak nobody is watching. Long-acting and ultra-long-acting Glargine (Lantus), detemir (Levemir) — relatively flat across roughly a day. Degludec (Tresiba) — essentially peakless and lasting beyond 24 hours, so doses overlap between days and a change takes several days to show its full effect. Flatness is the feature: a basal insulin is meant to have no peak to fall off. Premixed 70/30 and 75/25. A fixed ratio of an intermediate component and a rapid or short-acting component in one injection. Fewer injections, but the ratio is fixed — you cannot adjust the meal coverage without also moving the background insulin. That single constraint drives most of the trade-offs in the regimen table below. A practical bedside detail worth knowing cold NPH is cloudy. Regular and rapid-acting insulins are clear. It is a bedside safety check that costs nothing: if a vial that should be clear is cloudy, or a patient describes drawing up the wrong appearance, something has gone wrong before the injection. Thota S, Akbar A. Insulin. StatPearls [Internet]. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing. ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK560688 Classify The four regimens, and what each one costs the patient

entries.title: Regimen comparison
entries.text: The four commonly used regimens Every regimen buys something and pays for it somewhere else. The "major vulnerability" column is where the exam questions live. Regimen What it is Flexibility Meal timing Dose burden Major vulnerability Correct hyperglycemia? MDI / basal-bolus 1–2 basal injections (glargine, detemir, degludec) plus 2 or more mealtime injections (lispro, aspart, glulisine) High — carbohydrate amount is flexible Meal timing variable; basal needs consistent timing More than 4 injections daily ; snacks not required but may need their own insulin Number of injections, and the discipline it asks for Yes — even when not eating Pump / CSII Continuous basal infusion plus 2 or more boluses. Rapid-acting analog only. Highest — basal rates vary through the day; temporary basal rates for acute changes Fully flexible "One injection" every 3 days; worn 24 hours a day, brief disconnection allowed Technology fails. No long-acting depot, so an interruption becomes ketosis within hours. Higher expense. Yes , and most precisely — dosing in 0.025–0.05 unit increments Twice-daily (BID) 2 injections of intermediate insulin (NPH) mixed with rapid-acting or regular Low — a set amount of carbohydrate per meal Strict times for meals and injections; snacks must be eaten with the insulin peaks Fewer injections per day — this is the trade being made Activity and day-to-day variability make it hard; a peak arriving when food does not causes hypoglycemia Less likely Premixed 2 or more injections of 70/30 or 75/25 Lowest — the ratio of the two components is fixed Strict, as for BID Fewest decisions; simplest to teach You cannot move one component without moving the other Least likely of all — the fixed ratio makes an isolated correction the hardest to deliver of any regimen here Why the pump is described as the most physiological It is the only regimen that can change the basal rate by time of day — more insulin in the pre-dawn hours when counter-regulatory hormones are rising, less during an afternoon of exercise. A basal injection commits you to one profile for the whole 24 hours. Temporary basal rates allow acute adjustments for illness or activity, and the fine dosing increments make ratios and correction factors usable in a way pens cannot match. Why the pump's failure mode is the sharpest A pump contains rapid-acting insulin only . There is no long-acting depot underneath it. When delivery stops — occluded set, dislodged cannula, empty reservoir — the patient's entire insulin supply stops within a couple of hours, and ketosis follows quickly. This is why unexplained hyperglycemia on a pump prompts a check of the delivery system before any thought of adjusting doses. Donner T, Sarkar S. Insulin — Pharmacology, Therapeutic Regimens and Principles of Intensive Insulin Therapy. Endotext [Internet]. South Dartmouth (MA): MDText.com. ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK278938 Act The arithmetic, and then the pattern reading

entries.title: ICR, correction, target
entries.text: The three numbers a patient carries Insulin-to-carbohydrate ratio (ICR) The insulin required to cover the breakdown of carbohydrate into sugars and keep glucose in target. Written as "1 unit per XX grams." A larger XX is a weaker ratio. Correction factor (sensitivity factor) The insulin required to bring an out-of-range glucose down to target. Written as "1 unit decreases glucose by XX mg/dL." Basal insulin / basal rate, and target The insulin required to hold glucose at target when fasting or not eating . The target glucose is the number the correction aims at — corrections are calculated from the distance above it, which is why two patients with the same glucose can need different corrections. Retrieve Two patients both read 240 mg/dL. One has a correction factor of 1 unit per 25 mg/dL, the other 1 unit per 80. What does that difference tell you about them — before you calculate anything? The patient whose correction factor is 1 unit per 80 mg/dL is far more sensitive to insulin — a single unit moves their glucose a long way, so they need very few units to correct. The patient at 1 unit per 25 is much more insulin-resistant; each unit accomplishes less, so they need several times as many units for the same correction.

entries.title: Glucose pattern lab
entries.text: Glucose pattern lab The one principle this whole section teaches Evaluate the insulin that acted before the repeated abnormal pattern. Two words in that sentence do a lot of work. "Before" — you work backwards from the abnormal reading to whatever insulin was acting during the hours leading up to it, which is often not the insulin given nearest in time. "Repeated" — one bad day is a missed dose or an unusual meal, not a pattern. Confirm it repeats across several days before attributing it to an insulin period at all. Working the same logic on a twice-daily NPH regimen The reasoning is identical, but the answers change because the insulin shapes change. Read this table off the action curves rather than memorizing it — NPH given in the morning peaks in the afternoon, so it is the insulin covering the pre-dinner reading, and NPH given in the evening peaks overnight, so it is the insulin covering the fasting reading. Twice-daily NPH mixed with rapid-acting or regular insulin. This is an application of the action curves, not a separate rule to memorize. Glucose reading that is repeatedly abnormal Which insulin was acting before it Why Fasting / pre-breakfast Evening NPH Its broad peak falls across the overnight hours Pre-lunch Morning rapid-acting or regular The mealtime component given with breakfast covers the late morning Pre-dinner Morning NPH Injected at breakfast, it peaks through the afternoon Bedtime Evening rapid-acting or regular The mealtime component given with dinner covers the evening Why this table is a hazard as well as a tool Look at the fasting row. On a twice-daily regimen, a high fasting glucose points to the evening NPH — but so does an overnight low , because it is the same insulin peaking at the same hour. Raising the evening NPH to fix a morning high, without first checking what happened at three in the morning, is precisely the error the dawn phenomenon versus Somogyi distinction exists to prevent.

entries.title: Regimen cases
entries.text: Cases — reasoning across regimens Original cases written to cover the regimen types above. Each opens to a worked answer. Case 1 — MDI, morning highs Basal-bolus A college student with T1DM takes a long-acting basal insulin each morning, with an insulin-to-carbohydrate ratio of 1 unit per 4 g and a correction factor of 1 unit per 20 mg/dL above 120. They report consistent morning highs and want to increase the basal dose. What do you want to know, and what is the risk of simply agreeing? Work it through Reveal the reasoning Ask what the glucose does overnight — the pattern between bedtime and waking, over several days. A steady drift upward supports increasing the basal. A dip in the early hours followed by a rebound means more basal would deepen a nocturnal hypoglycemia. Then notice the timing. The basal is taken in the morning . Long-acting analogs are relatively flat but not perfectly so, and their weakest coverage tends to fall at the far end of the dosing interval — which here is the overnight period. So the question is not only how much basal but when it is given. And check the bedtime bolus. A very strong ratio of 1 unit per 4 g means a large evening dose, and insulin still active from it changes the overnight picture. Look at the whole night before touching a standing dose. Case 2 — premixed insulin and a mid-afternoon low Premixed A young adult with long-standing T1DM has switched from MDI to a premixed 70/30 regimen, taking a larger morning dose and a smaller evening dose, because the injection burden had become unmanageable. They now report lows in the mid-afternoon and highs before bed. What is happening, and what does the regimen make difficult? Work it through Reveal the reasoning The mid-afternoon low is the intermediate component of the morning injection peaking — a large morning dose means a large afternoon peak, arriving whether or not the patient eats. This is the reason twice-daily regimens require snacks timed to the insulin peaks . The pre-bed high is the evening injection's rapid component being too small for the evening meal. The bind: the 70/30 ratio is fixed. Reducing the morning dose to fix the afternoon low also reduces the morning meal coverage. Increasing the evening dose to cover dinner also increases the overnight intermediate component. You cannot move one component without moving the other — which is the trade the patient accepted in exchange for fewer injections. Recognizing that the regimen, not the patient, is generating the pattern is the clinical point. Case 3 — pump user, A1c rising after a job change CSII An adult with T1DM on pump therapy with continuous glucose monitoring has held an A1c below 7.0% for years. It has risen to 8.1% since starting a new job. The pump is functioning and sets are being changed on schedule. Where do you look? Work it through Reveal the reasoning At the pattern, by time of day, and specifically at whether boluses are being given at all. A pump's great advantage — that a bolus is a few button presses rather than an injection — is also the easiest thing to postpone during a busy day and then forget. Missed or late mealtime boluses are among the most common reasons an established pump user's control drifts, and the bolus history in the pump answers the question directly. Then ask what else changed with the job: meal timing, meal content, activity level, sleep, and stress. A regimen that worked for one daily rhythm may need different basal rates for a different one — which the pump can accommodate, once you know which hours are the problem. Note what this case is not : the sets are being changed and the pump works, so this is not a delivery failure. Delivery failure looks like the pump-interruption trace in the pattern lab — a rapid, unrelenting rise over hours, not a gradual drift in A1c over months. Case 4 — hypoglycemia unawareness Safety An older adult with long-standing T1DM and known hypoglycemia unawareness is on a twice-daily NPH and regular regimen. Why

entries.text: What this session asks of you The seven stated objectives, and where each one is answered 1. Why ignoring cholesterol's carbon numbering is a mistake → the numbering is the map . 2. Compare and contrast the pathways and their locations → the pathway and zone-specific synthesis . 3. The puzzle of one gene, one polypeptide, two activities, and why only 17α-hydroxylation is needed for cortisol → the CYP17A1 problem . 4. A rationale for calling glucocorticoid-remediable aldosteronism a design flaw in the genome → the design flaw . 5. Etymology and pathophysiology of glucocorticoid-remediable aldosteronism → what the name is telling you . 6. A mechanism by which 21-hydroxylase deficiency produces atypical genitalia in XX infants → from a missing enzyme to a virilized fetus . 7. Classical versus non-classical congenital adrenal hyperplasia by symptomatology → classic and non-classic, side by side . The one sentence version Cholesterol (27 carbons) is cut down to pregnenolone (21 carbons), and from there three branches diverge: keep 21 carbons and you get mineralocorticoids and glucocorticoids ; cut the side chain to 19 carbons and you get androgens ; remove one more carbon and aromatize the A ring to 18 carbons and you get estrogens . The habit worth building now When you meet any steroid disorder, ask three questions in this order: is cortisol low (so ACTH is high and the gland is hyperplastic), is there salt wasting or hypertension (the mineralocorticoid arm), and are androgens high or low (the sex-steroid arm). Those three answers name the enzyme without your having to recall a list.

entries.title: Carbons and why they matter
entries.text: The numbering is the map, not a decoration Objective 1 asks you to explain to a colleague why skipping the carbon numbering is a mistake. Here is the argument. The point in one line Almost every enzyme in steroidogenesis is named after the carbon it acts on . If the numbers mean nothing to you, the enzyme names are arbitrary syllables and the pathway becomes rote. If the numbers mean something, the name of the enzyme tells you the reaction , and the reaction tells you what accumulates when it fails. Read the name, predict the chemistry. Every one of these is a carbon position doing exactly what it says. Enzyme What the name literally says Consequence for the molecule Cholesterol side-chain cleavage — 20,22-desmolase Cut the bond between C20 and C22 Removes six carbons of the tail. C27 cholesterol → C21 pregnenolone. This is the committed step of all steroidogenesis. 17α-hydroxylase Add an OH at C17 , α face Opens the door to cortisol and to androgens. No carbons are lost — the molecule is still C21. 17,20-lyase Cut the bond between C17 and C20 Removes the two-carbon acetyl side chain. C21 → C19. This is the step that makes something an androgen. 21-hydroxylase Add an OH at C21 Required for both cortisol and aldosterone. Lose it and you lose both arms at once — which is exactly why its deficiency is the dangerous one. 11β-hydroxylase Add an OH at C11 , β face The last step to cortisol. Note that hydroxylating C11 creates a new asymmetric carbon, which is why the α/β designation is not optional. Aldosterone synthase Acts at C11 and then C18 — hydroxylation then oxidation Converts corticosterone → 18-hydroxycorticosterone → aldosterone, whose defining feature is the C18 aldehyde. Aromatase Removes C19 and aromatizes ring A C19 androgen → C18 estrogen. The lost methyl group and the aromatic A ring are the whole structural difference between testosterone and estradiol. 5α-reductase Reduces the double bond at C5 , α face Testosterone → dihydrotestosterone. Same carbon count, dramatically higher receptor affinity. 3β- and 17β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase Oxidize or reduce the oxygen at C3 or C17 3β-HSD converts Δ5 steroids to Δ4 — the switch from the pregnenolone series to the progesterone series. 17β-HSD is the last step to testosterone and to estradiol. Say this to your colleague "You cannot tell 17α-hydroxylase from 17,20-lyase without the numbers, and those two are the same protein doing different jobs. You cannot explain why 21-hydroxylase deficiency wrecks both cortisol and aldosterone but 11β-hydroxylase deficiency causes hypertension, unless you know where C21 and C11 sit relative to each other in the sequence. And you cannot explain why an androgen becomes an estrogen without knowing that C19 is the carbon that leaves. The numbering is not nomenclature — it is the mechanism written down." C21 — pregnanes Progesterone, 11-deoxycorticosterone, corticosterone, aldosterone, 11-deoxycortisol, cortisol. The full side chain is still attached. C19 — androstanes DHEA, androstenedione, testosterone, dihydrotestosterone. The 17,20-lyase step removed the side chain. C18 — estranes Estrone, estradiol. Aromatase removed the C19 methyl and made ring A aromatic.

entries.title: The enzyme cast
entries.text: The cast: cytochrome P450s and dehydrogenases Two chemical families, two subcellular addresses. Knowing which is which explains why the intermediates shuttle in and out of the mitochondrion. Cytochrome P450s — the hydroxylases Heme mono-oxygenases. They insert an oxygen atom, consuming O₂ and NADPH through a redox partner. The mitochondrial ones (CYP11A1, CYP11B1, CYP11B2) use ferredoxin and ferredoxin reductase; the ones in the smooth endoplasmic reticulum (CYP17A1, CYP21A2, CYP19A1) use P450 oxidoreductase. Every enzyme whose name contains "hydroxylase," "desmolase," "lyase," or "aromatase" is a P450. Hydroxysteroid dehydrogenases Not P450s and not heme proteins. They move a hydrogen using NAD⁺/NADH or NADP⁺/NADPH , interconverting a hydroxyl group and a ketone. 3β-HSD (HSD3B2) and 17β-HSD (HSD17B) are the two you need. They are freely reversible in principle, which is why tissue expression of a particular isoform decides the direction. The full cast, with the gene name and the compartment. Abbreviations in the left column are the ones used in the pathway map below. Short form Enzyme Gene Where it works StAR Steroidogenic acute regulatory protein — not an enzyme; a transporter STAR Moves cholesterol from the outer to the inner mitochondrial membrane. The rate-limiting step. SCC Cholesterol side-chain cleavage (20,22-desmolase) CYP11A1 Inner mitochondrial membrane 3β 3β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase / Δ5→Δ4 isomerase HSD3B2 Smooth ER and mitochondria 17α 17α-hydroxylase activity of CYP17A1 CYP17A1 Smooth ER lyase 17,20-lyase activity of the same CYP17A1 protein — requires cytochrome b5 CYP17A1 Smooth ER 21 21-hydroxylase CYP21A2 Smooth ER 11β 11β-hydroxylase CYP11B1 Inner mitochondrial membrane, zona fasciculata AS Aldosterone synthase (11β-hydroxylase, 18-hydroxylase and 18-oxidase activities in one protein) CYP11B2 Inner mitochondrial membrane, zona glomerulosa only 17β 17β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase HSD17B Gonads and peripheral tissue arom Aromatase CYP19A1 Ovarian granulosa cells, placenta, adipose tissue, brain, bone 5α 5α-reductase SRD5A2 Genital skin, prostate, hair follicle — a peripheral enzyme, not an adrenal one SULT2A1 / STS Sulfotransferase and steroid sulfatase — interconvert DHEA and DHEA-sulfate SULT2A1, STS Zona reticularis and periphery. DHEA-S is the long-lived circulating reservoir and the practical marker of adrenal androgen output. Two naming points that catch people out The lecture slides write the 21-hydroxylase gene as CYP21A1 . In current gene nomenclature the functional gene is CYP21A2 , on chromosome 6p21.3 inside the HLA class III region; CYP21A1P is the neighbouring non-functional pseudogene, and the fact that a working gene sits beside a broken near-copy is precisely why most CAH alleles arise by gene conversion or deletion. Second: aldosterone synthase and 11β-hydroxylase are separate gene products (CYP11B2 and CYP11B1) that both carry 11β-hydroxylase activity — remember that and the chimeric-gene disease later on will make sense.

entries.title: The pathway map
entries.text: The whole map on one grid Three columns, three products. Read left to right for the branch, top to bottom for the sequence. The steroidogenic pathway arranged as three branches Cholesterol is converted by side-chain cleavage to pregnenolone. Pregnenolone can go three ways. Down, via 3-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase, to progesterone and then along the mineralocorticoid branch: 21-hydroxylase makes 11-deoxycorticosterone, 11-beta-hydroxylase makes corticosterone, and aldosterone synthase makes 18-hydroxycorticosterone and then aldosterone. Right, via 17-alpha-hydroxylase, to 17-hydroxypregnenolone and 17-hydroxyprogesterone, and then along the glucocorticoid branch: 21-hydroxylase makes 11-deoxycortisol and 11-beta-hydroxylase makes cortisol. Right again, via 17,20-lyase, to dehydroepiandrosterone and androstenedione, and then along the androgen branch: 17-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase makes testosterone, 5-alpha-reductase makes dihydrotestosterone, and aromatase makes estradiol. mineralocorticoid glucocorticoid androgen / estrogen cholesterol SCC StAR moves cholesterol into the mitochondrion — the rate-limiting step of every steroid below pregnenolone 17-OH-pregnenolone DHEA 17α lyase 3β 3β 3β progesterone 17-OH-progesterone androstenedione 17α lyase 21 21 17β 11-deoxycorticosterone 11-deoxycortisol testosterone 11β 11β 5α corticosterone cortisol dihydrotestosterone AS arom 18-OH-corticosterone estradiol AS aldosterone zona glomerulosa zona fasciculata zona reticularis CYP11B2, no CYP17A1 CYP17A1 but no b5 CYP17A1 with b5 shaded boxes are the biologically active end products · the top two rows are common to all three zones Original diagram, drawn from the pathway presented in the session. The vertical axis is the sequence and the horizontal axis is the branch point : every step to the right removes or modifies carbons at C17, every step downward adds oxygen at C21, C11, or C18. Two structural facts to carry away — 21-hydroxylase serves both the left and the middle column , which is why its loss is the most damaging single deficiency, and 17α-hydroxylase is the gate to both the middle and the right column , which is why its loss removes cortisol and all sex steroids at once while leaving the left column not merely intact but overdriven. Trace three paths out loud before moving on To aldosterone: cholesterol → pregnenolone → progesterone → 11-deoxycorticosterone → corticosterone → 18-hydroxycorticosterone → aldosterone. To cortisol: cholesterol → pregnenolone → 17-OH-pregnenolone → 17-OH-progesterone → 11-deoxycortisol → cortisol. To testosterone: cholesterol → pregnenolone → 17-OH-pregnenolone → DHEA → androstenedione → testosterone, then 5α-reductase to DHT or aromatase to estradiol in the periphery.

entries.title: Three zones, three products
entries.text: Why each zone makes only its own hormone Same genome in every cell of the cortex. What differs is which steroidogenic enzymes are transcribed — and that is the whole explanation. Zona glomerulosa — 10–15% Aldosterone. Expresses CYP11B2 (aldosterone synthase) and does not express CYP17A1 . With no 17α-hydroxylation available, everything is forced down the mineralocorticoid branch. Driven by angiotensin II and potassium , not primarily by ACTH. Zona fasciculata — 70–80% Cortisol. Expresses CYP17A1 , plus CYP21A2 and CYP11B1 , but not cytochrome b5 — so it performs 17α-hydroxylation without the subsequent lyase step. Driven by ACTH . The largest zone, because cortisol output dwarfs everything else the cortex makes. Zona reticularis — 10–15% DHEA, DHEA-S, androstenedione. Expresses CYP17A1 with cytochrome b5 , so the lyase activity runs; relatively low 3β-HSD , which favours DHEA; and SULT2A1 , which sulfates it. Carries receptors for ACTH and also for LH and FSH, all of which raise cAMP. A mnemonic, and the thing it does not tell you Salt, sugar, sex — the deeper you go, the sweeter it gets: glomerulosa → salt, fasciculata → sugar, reticularis → sex. What it does not capture is the mechanism: the difference between the zones is enzyme expression, not anatomy . The medulla is a separate story entirely — neural crest in origin, chromaffin cells making catecholamines, and it appears on the adrenal disorders page as the home of pheochromocytoma. Adrenal androgens are weak, and that matters DHEA and androstenedione are the adrenal's androgen products and both are weak ; potency comes from peripheral and gonadal conversion to testosterone and DHT . They dominate androgen exposure before puberty in both sexes . After puberty the gonads take over in males, while in females the adrenal remains a major androgen source — which is why adrenal androgen excess is a much bigger clinical problem in girls and women. And why the fetus is the vulnerable one Pathologically raised adrenal androgens have a far greater effect on 46,XX development before puberty, and above all in utero , than on 46,XY development — an XY fetus is already awash in testicular testosterone, so extra adrenal androgen changes little, whereas an XX fetus has a bipotential external genital anlage that responds to it. Hold on to that asymmetry; it is the whole of objective 6 .

entries.title: The CYP17A1 puzzle
entries.text: One gene, one polypeptide, two activities Objective 3 asks you to puzzle over this deliberately. It rewards the effort, because the answer explains the zonation you just learned. The apparent paradox CYP17A1 is a single gene encoding a single polypeptide that carries two catalytic activities : 17α-hydroxylase and 17,20-lyase. Adrenal androgen synthesis needs both — you must hydroxylate C17 and then cleave the C17–C20 bond. Cortisol synthesis needs only the first . So how does one protein, present in both the fasciculata and the reticularis, run both reactions in one zone and only one reaction in the other? Cytochrome b5 as the switch between the two CYP17A1 activities In the zona fasciculata, CYP17A1 converts progesterone to 17-hydroxyprogesterone and stops there, because cytochrome b5 is absent; 21-hydroxylase and 11-beta-hydroxylase then carry it on to cortisol. In the zona reticularis, cytochrome b5 is present, so the same enzyme continues past 17-hydroxyprogesterone and cleaves the C17 to C20 bond, producing androstenedione. progesterone 17α 17-OH-progesterone the branch point 21 → 11β cortisol zona fasciculata — no b5 lyase + b5 androstenedione zona reticularis — b5 present The same protein, the same substrate. Only the partner protein differs. Original diagram. Cytochrome b5 is the switch. It is not a substrate and not the catalytic enzyme — it is an allosteric partner that promotes the electron transfer the lyase reaction needs. Where b5 is expressed (zona reticularis) CYP17A1 carries straight on through to a C19 androgen; where it is not (zona fasciculata) the reaction stops at 17-hydroxyprogesterone and 21- and 11β-hydroxylase take the molecule to cortisol instead. The resolution, stated plainly The two activities are separably regulated even though they are inseparably encoded . 17α-hydroxylase runs wherever CYP17A1 is expressed. 17,20-lyase additionally requires cytochrome b5 (and serine phosphorylation of the enzyme, and an adequate supply of electrons from P450 oxidoreductase). Control the partner and you control which of the two reactions the cell actually performs. Why this is worth the effort It explains adrenarche — the rise in adrenal androgens at around age 6 to 8, independent of gonadarche, which tracks maturation of the zona reticularis and its b5 expression rather than any change in ACTH. It also explains why CYP17A1 deficiency takes out cortisol and all sex steroids together, while leaving the mineralocorticoid arm not just intact but over-supplied.

entries.title: Regulation of each branch
entries.text: Two separate control systems in one gland Separate control of the cortisol and aldosterone branches On the left, the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus releases CRH to the pituitary, which releases ACTH; ACTH acts on the MC2 receptor of the zona fasciculata through a G-alpha-s protein and cAMP and PKA, producing cortisol, which feeds back negatively on both the pituitary and the hypothalamus. On the right, angiotensin II and potassium act on the zona glomerulosa through the AT1 receptor and G-q, raising intracellular calcium and inducing aldosterone synthase, producing aldosterone. Cortisol branch — ACTH Aldosterone branch — renin–angiotensin and K⁺ hypothalamus — CRH pituitary — ACTH zona fasciculata MC2R → Gαs → cAMP → PKA cortisol negative feedback ↓ renal perfusion → renin → angiotensin II · or ↑ K⁺ zona glomerulosa AT1R → Gq → ↑ Ca²⁺ ↑ CYP11B2 transcription aldosterone ACTH contributes, but is not the main driver Original diagram. Two branches, two second messengers: cAMP on the left, calcium on the right . Keeping them separate is what lets you predict which hormone is lost in which disease — and it is exactly this separation that glucocorticoid-remediable aldosteronism destroys. ACTH acts on two timescales Short term (minutes): cAMP/PKA phosphorylates and mobilizes StAR , and cholesterol esters — largely from serum LDL taken up by the cell — are moved into the mitochondrion. This is where the rate-limiting step is regulated. Long term (hours to days): cAMP-responsive transcription factors induce StAR and the steroidogenic enzymes themselves , and the cortex grows. That second mechanism is why chronically high ACTH produces hyperplasia — the "H" in congenital adrenal hyperplasia. What drives ACTH Diurnal rhythm — peak in the early morning, trough around midnight; this is the basis of the late-night salivary cortisol test on the adrenal page . And stress — illness, injury, surgery, hypoglycemia. Negative feedback by cortisol closes the loop at both the pituitary and the hypothalamus, which is why exogenous glucocorticoid suppresses the whole axis. Sex steroid production — the two-cell model Ovary: LH drives the theca cell , which has CYP17A1 and makes androstenedione; androstenedione crosses to the granulosa cell , where FSH drives aromatase and it becomes estrone and then estradiol. Neither cell can do the whole job alone. After the LH surge the theca cells luteinize, CYP17A1 expression falls sharply, and progesterone becomes the major product — which is the biochemistry of the luteal phase. Testis: LH drives the Leydig cell to make testosterone, which is then converted peripherally to DHT by 5α-reductase or to estradiol by aromatase .

entries.title: GRA — the design flaw
entries.text: Glucocorticoid-remediable aldosteronism: building the "design flaw" argument Objective 4 asks you to construct a rationale, not to recite a fact. Here is the chain of reasoning, one link at a time. Unequal crossing over between CYP11B1 and CYP11B2 creates a chimeric gene Two homologous chromosome 8s each carry CYP11B1 and CYP11B2 side by side. Because the two genes are nearly identical in sequence, they can misalign during meiosis, so that CYP11B1 on one chromosome pairs with CYP11B2 on the other. A crossover in that misaligned region produces one chromosome carrying a chimeric gene with the CYP11B1 promoter fused to CYP11B2 coding sequence, and a reciprocal chromosome carrying the CYP11B2 promoter fused to CYP11B1 coding sequence. The first is the cause of glucocorticoid-remediable aldosteronism; the second is clinically silent. Normal chromosome 8q24.3 — two near-identical genes in tandem CYP11B1 CYP11B2 ≈95% identical coding sequence Misalignment in meiosis, then a crossover CYP11B1 CYP11B2 CYP11B1 CYP11B2 the recombination machinery cannot reliably tell the two copies apart Two reciprocal products B1 promoter + B2 coding aldosterone synthase driven by ACTH B2 promoter + B1 coding 11β-hydroxylase driven by angiotensin II disease — GRA clinically insignificant cortisol output ≈10–20 mg/day · aldosterone output ≈0.05–0.2 mg/day — the asymmetry is the reason Original diagram. The reciprocal products of the same crossover have wildly different consequences. Putting a small hormone system under a large drive is a catastrophe; putting a large system under a small additional drive changes nothing measurable. The argument, link by link 1. CYP11B2 arose from CYP11B1 by gene duplication. Getting a dedicated aldosterone synthase, separately regulated from cortisol synthesis, was an evolutionary gain. 2. The duplicates were left sitting next to each other on chromosome 8q24.3, ~95% identical in their coding regions. The genome never tidied up. 3. Meiotic recombination works by pairing homologous sequence. It is a sequence-matching process; it has no concept of gene identity. 4. Therefore CYP11B1 on one chromosome can pair with CYP11B2 on the other. Near-identity is indistinguishable from identity as far as the machinery is concerned. 5. A crossover in that misaligned pairing yields a chimeric gene — the promoter of one fused to the coding sequence of the other. 6. The chimera with the CYP11B1 promoter and CYP11B2 coding sequence places aldosterone synthase under ACTH control and expresses it in the zona fasciculata. Disease. 7. Therefore the flaw is structural, not mutational : nothing was damaged, no base was mis-copied. The arrangement of the genome itself makes this error recurrent — and that is what justifies calling it a design flaw rather than bad luck. The same flaw, a second time The strongest support for the argument is that the genome does it again. CYP21A2 sits beside the non-functional pseudogene CYP21A1P in the same head-to-tail arrangement, and most disease-causing 21-hydroxylase alleles arise not from spontaneous point mutation but from gene conversion or deletion between the gene and its pseudogene . Two of the most important disorders in this session — GRA and congenital adrenal hyperplasia — share one root cause: near-identical sequences kept in tandem .

entries.title: GRA — name and disease
entries.text: What the name "glucocorticoid-remediable" is telling you Objective 5: dissect the etymology, then the pathophysiology. The name is unusually informative — it names the treatment, not the lesion. The etymology, word by word Hyper-aldosteron-ism — too much aldosterone. Remediable — from remedium , able to be remedied; the condition is corrected by the thing named. Glucocorticoid — the class of drug that corrects it. So: hyperaldosteronism that a glucocorticoid fixes . The trap the name sets is that it sounds like a glucocorticoid deficiency state. It is not. The glucocorticoid is being given as a suppressant of ACTH , not as replacement. It is also known as familial hyperaldosteronism type 1 (FH-I) , and inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern. The pathophysiology in five steps 1. The chimeric gene expresses aldosterone synthase activity in the zona fasciculata , where it does not belong. 2. It is transcribed from the CYP11B1 promoter , so it answers to ACTH . 3. Aldosterone production therefore follows the ACTH rhythm rather than renin, angiotensin II, or potassium. 4. Aldosterone excess → sodium retention → volume expansion → hypertension , with hypokalemia and suppressed renin (volume expansion switches the renin–angiotensin system off). 5. Give dexamethasone : ACTH is suppressed, the abnormal drive is removed, and aldosterone normalizes. The response is not just treatment — it is the diagnostic demonstration. Recognizing it clinically, and how it is confirmed Suspect it in early-onset hypertension with a family history of hypertension or of hemorrhagic stroke before age 40 , especially with hypokalemia and a raised aldosterone-to-renin ratio. Because the fasciculata is now hydroxylating cortisol at C18, patients excrete the hybrid steroids 18-oxocortisol and 18-hydroxycortisol , which are characteristic. Confirmation today is genetic testing for the chimeric gene rather than a dexamethasone trial. Treatment is a low-dose glucocorticoid to suppress ACTH, a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist , or both. It is rare — a small percentage of primary aldosteronism — but it is the one form with a mechanism you can derive from first principles, which is why it is on the syllabus. Lifton RP et al. A chimaeric 11β-hydroxylase/aldosterone synthase gene causes glucocorticoid-remediable aldosteronism and human hypertension. Nature 1992; and OMIM #103900, Hyperaldosteronism, Familial, Type I. omim.org/entry/103900

entries.title: 21-OHD → virilization
entries.text: From a missing enzyme to a virilized XX fetus Objective 6 asks you to formulate the mechanism. Six steps, each one following from the last. The consequences of a 21-hydroxylase block A block at 21-hydroxylase stops both the aldosterone and the cortisol branches. Cortisol falls, which removes negative feedback so ACTH rises, which both enlarges the adrenal cortex and drives more precursor into the pathway. 17-hydroxyprogesterone accumulates above the block and is diverted through 17,20-lyase into androstenedione and then testosterone and dihydrotestosterone, producing virilization of a 46,XX fetus. Aldosterone loss produces salt wasting. 17-OH-progesterone 21-hydroxylase blocked ↓ cortisol · ↓ aldosterone lost feedback → ↑ ACTH adrenal hyperplasia + more substrate in salt wasting ↓Na⁺ ↑K⁺ shock lyase androstenedione testosterone → DHT virilization of the 46,XX external genitalia the only exit still open one block, three consequences — and the loop feeds itself Original diagram. The feature that makes this pathway self-amplifying is the feedback arm: the missing cortisol raises ACTH, and higher ACTH pushes still more substrate into a pathway whose only open exit is the androgen branch. That is why an untreated infant does not simply have low cortisol — they have enormous androgen production. The mechanism in six steps 1. 21-hydroxylase converts 17-OH-progesterone → 11-deoxycortisol and progesterone → 11-deoxycorticosterone. It therefore serves both the cortisol and the aldosterone arms. 2. Lose it and cortisol and aldosterone both fall . 3. Low cortisol removes negative feedback, so ACTH rises — acutely mobilizing cholesterol, chronically inducing enzymes and enlarging the cortex (the hyperplasia of the name). 4. Substrate piles up immediately above the block, so 17-OH-progesterone rises steeply . 5. The only route still open to that backlog is 17,20-lyase → DHEA and androstenedione, which are converted peripherally to testosterone and DHT . 6. A 46,XX fetus has a bipotential external genital anlage that responds to androgen. Exposure before about 12 weeks produces labioscrotal fusion and a urogenital sinus; exposure after about 12–14 weeks , once the structures are formed, produces clitoromegaly without fusion. Why the internal structures are unaffected — and why this matters The affected fetus has ovaries, a uterus, and fallopian tubes, all normal . Adrenal androgen does not produce Müllerian regression, because that requires AMH from Sertoli cells , and there are none. Nor does it stabilize the Wolffian ducts, which need high local testosterone from an adjacent testis rather than circulating androgen. So the virilization is external only — which is exactly why these children are fertile and are raised female, and why the finding is correctable. The clinical consequences are worked through on the DSD page .

entries.title: Classic vs non-classic CAH
entries.text: Classic and non-classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia Objective 7. One gene, a spectrum of residual enzyme activity, and a presentation that tracks that residue almost linearly. The organizing idea The three forms are not three diseases. They are one enzyme deficiency at three severities . Ask how much 21-hydroxylase activity is left and everything else follows: near-zero activity loses cortisol and aldosterone; a little activity keeps aldosterone but not cortisol; a lot of activity keeps both under basal conditions and only shows up as androgen excess later in life. 21-hydroxylase deficiency accounts for roughly 90–95% of all congenital adrenal hyperplasia. Classic — salt-wasting Classic — simple virilizing Non-classic Residual enzyme activity Essentially none (<1–2%) A little (roughly 1–5%) Substantial (roughly 20–50%) Cortisol Deficient Deficient Adequate at baseline Aldosterone Deficient — salt wasting Preserved Preserved When it presents First 1–3 weeks of life, as an adrenal crisis At birth in 46,XX; later in 46,XY as early virilization Childhood, adolescence, or adulthood — sometimes never Genitalia at birth 46,XX atypical; 46,XY normal-appearing 46,XX atypical; 46,XY normal-appearing Normal in both Characteristic symptoms Vomiting, poor feeding, failure to thrive, dehydration, hypotension, shock, hypoglycemia, hyponatremia with hyperkalemia Rapid somatic growth, advanced bone age with a short adult height, premature pubic hair, acne, virilization Premature adrenarche, hirsutism, acne, oligomenorrhea, a PCOS-like picture, subfertility — or no symptoms at all Approximate frequency Classic overall about 1 in 14,000–18,000 births; roughly three-quarters of classic cases are salt-wasting Far commoner — of the order of 1 in 200 to 1 in 1,000, and higher in some populations How each is found Classic: the newborn screen measures 17-hydroxyprogesterone , which is why an affected 46,XY infant — who looks entirely normal at birth and would otherwise present in shock — is caught before the crisis. Non-classic: an early-morning, follicular-phase 17-OHP ; if that is borderline, an ACTH (cosyntropin) stimulation test unmasks it. Genotyping confirms. How each is treated Classic: hydrocortisone for glucocorticoid replacement, fludrocortisone plus sodium chloride supplementation for the mineralocorticoid arm, and stress dosing during illness. Goals are to prevent crisis while normalizing growth and androgens — over-treating stunts growth, under-treating advances bone age. Non-classic: often no treatment ; glucocorticoid only if symptomatic androgen excess or fertility problems warrant it. The other blocks, in one line each 11β-hydroxylase deficiency — the second commonest: androgens high, cortisol low, but 11-deoxycorticosterone accumulates and, being a weak mineralocorticoid in large amounts, causes hypertension and hypokalemia . Virilizing and hypertensive. 17α-hydroxylase/17,20-lyase deficiency — no cortisol and no sex steroids, but DOC and corticosterone accumulate: hypertension with absent puberty , and an undervirilized 46,XY infant. 3β-HSD deficiency — Δ5 steroids accumulate; DHEA is a weak androgen, so 46,XX infants are mildly virilized and 46,XY infants are undervirilized. It is the one form in which both sexes can have atypical genitalia. The full enzyme-by-enzyme lab table is on the adrenal disorders page . Speiser PW et al. Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia Due to Steroid 21-Hydroxylase Deficiency: An Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline. J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2018;103(11):4043–4088. academic.oup.com/jcem/article/103/11/4043 · Nimkarn S et al. 21-Hydroxylase-Deficient Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia. entries.title: Retrieval prompts
entries.text: Retrieval prompts Answer out loud before opening each one. Retrieve Why does 21-hydroxylase deficiency cause both salt wasting and virilization, while 17α-hydroxylase deficiency causes hypertension and no virilization? Position in the pathway. 21-hydroxylase sits on the mineralocorticoid and the glucocorticoid arms but not on the androgen arm, so its loss removes aldosterone and cortisol while leaving the androgen exit open for the accumulating precursor — salt wasting plus virilization. 17α-hydroxylase sits at the gate to the glucocorticoid and androgen arms, so its loss removes cortisol and all sex steroids while diverting everything into the mineralocorticoid arm — DOC and corticosterone accumulate, giving hypertension with hypokalemia and no virilization. Retrieve One gene, one protein, two activities. Say precisely what decides whether CYP17A1 performs one reaction or both. Cytochrome b5. The 17α-hydroxylase reaction runs wherever CYP17A1 is expressed. The 17,20-lyase reaction additionally requires cytochrome b5 as an allosteric partner promoting electron transfer. b5 is expressed in the zona reticularis and not the zona fasciculata , so the reticularis makes androgens while the fasciculata stops at 17-hydroxyprogesterone and goes on to cortisol. The genetics are inseparable; the regulation is not. Retrieve Why is the reciprocal chimeric gene — CYP11B2 promoter with CYP11B1 coding sequence — clinically silent? Scale. Cortisol output is of the order of 10–20 mg per day; aldosterone output is of the order of 0.05–0.2 mg per day — a difference of roughly two orders of magnitude. Adding a little angiotensin-II-driven 11β-hydroxylase to an already large cortisol system is undetectable. Putting the tiny aldosterone system under the large, tonic ACTH drive transforms it. Same crossover, same two products, opposite clinical significance. Retrieve A 22-year-old woman has hirsutism, acne, and irregular periods. Her morning 17-OHP is mildly raised. What is the diagnosis, and what would have been true at her birth? Non-classic 21-hydroxylase deficiency , which mimics PCOS. At birth she had normal genitalia and a normal newborn screen , because 20–50% residual enzyme activity is enough for normal cortisol and aldosterone under basal conditions and enough to keep fetal androgen exposure below the threshold for virilization. Confirm with an early-morning follicular-phase 17-OHP, and use an ACTH stimulation test if the value is equivocal.
